title: Lesson 37: CI/CD for Agents: Prompt Versioning, Model Registries, and Canary Releases
description: Turning agent tests into a release pipeline: versioning prompts as immutable artifacts, pinning models in a registry, and rolling changes out as measurable canaries with a rollback that is a routing change.

questions.question: Why does an agent break the assumption behind conventional CI/CD?
options: Its behavior is shaped by code, model, prompts, and data at once
Its full test suite takes too long to run on every commit
Its dependencies cannot be pinned inside a build artifact
Its behavior is fully determined by application code alone and never changes
questions.explanation: An agent's behavior is shaped by the model, the prompts, and the retrieved data as well as the code, and any of them can change without a single line of application code changing.

questions.question: How should a canary release of a new prompt behave for a conversational agent?
options: Compare the canary against a historical monthly baseline and redeploy to roll back
Route each request independently so traffic mixes freely between both versions
Split a small slice of traffic and compare the two versions against each other
Wait for full rollout before scoring any quality metric from the canary
questions.explanation: The canary and the stable version run concurrently and are compared with each other, rollback is an instant routing change rather than a redeploy, and conversational agents are pinned by session.

questions.question: What does pinning a model registry version in the build give you?
options: A guarantee that the provider will never change the model version underneath you
A reproducible artifact, so a week-old build behaves as it did when tested
A replacement for the evaluation dataset as evidence of quality
An automatic rewrite of prompts when their quality drifts
questions.explanation: Pinning the model registry version, each prompt revision, and the provider API version makes the build reproducible, so an old artifact still behaves as it did when it was tested.
